title: Zillow Observed Rent Index (ZORI): monthly asking-rent change in the ten largest metros, plus a top-10 ranking
brief: Revision 2 records the owner's decisions: on rights, a person asks Zillow Research and work waits. If there is no answer by 2026-12-18, the fallback is the BLS metro rent profile. Both questions run (Q1 ten-metro profile, Q2 top-10 ranking), with the doc's lock, and the file comes by browser download only. Each month, entrants forecast the seasonally adjusted one-month % change in Zillow's asking-rent index (ZORI) for the ten largest metros, and rank the ten fastest-rising of the 50 largest. A named person downloads the CSV by hand, and an ingest tool checks, hashes and files it privately; rounds resolve on that copy. Work waits on Zillow's written answer, which a maintainer sends (text drafted in Source). After that come two unscored pilot rounds, which also measure the reference's spread. So the earliest scored lock is about early March 2027 (February data), if the answer comes by 2026-12-18. The rights verdict, permission needed, is proposed for maintainers.
question: Q1 (profile): what will be the seasonally adjusted month-over-month % change in ZORI (All Homes Plus Multifamily, smoothed, seasonally adjusted) from month M-1 to month M for each of the ten largest metros by Zillow SizeRank (New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, Dallas, Houston, Washington, Philadelphia, Miami, Atlanta, Boston), computed within the first archived Zillow file whose newest column is M? Q2 (ranking): which ten of the 50 largest metros will have the highest such change in month M, in order?

source.access: Browser download only (owner decision, rev 2); no script, scraper or scheduled fetch touches any Zillow host. Who: one named person, by default the track owner (mingyihe@mit.edu), with one named SSA maintainer as backup, both recorded in the round file. Neither name is chosen by the agent. What: in a normal browser, open https://www.zillow.com/research/data/, section 'Rentals', data type 'ZORI (Smoothed, Seasonally Adjusted): All Homes Plus Multifamily Time Series ($)', geography 'Metro & U.S.', then Download. The browser saves Metro_zori_uc_sfrcondomfr_sm_sa_month.csv, served from https://files.zillowstatic.com/research/public_csvs/zori/ [owner doc; the SA file name is not in the 2026-10-26 Internet Archive capture of the page, which links only the not-SA file Metro_zori_uc_sfrcondomfr_sm_month.csv, so it is unverified]. When: once a month, from the 16th 00:00 ET, when Zillow's calendar says monthly data update (the owner measured landings at 13:45 ET on 2025-06-16 and 22:11 ET on 2026-09-15). Target the 16th to 18th. The ingest tool refuses a file whose newest column is not the expected month, so downloading too early is harmless. One download a month serves two rounds: it resolves round M and is the lock reference for round M+1, which locks in early M+2. Then: run the ingest tool (below) on the saved file and commit the result under the private archive. Ingest tool, to be written: tools/ingest_zori.py <file> --expected-month YYYY-MM [--capture-day], modelled on tools/ingest_yougov_xtab.py (origin/dev). Like that tool, it reads only a local file and never fetches. Checks, each a hard stop with 'archive unchanged': (a) the file name is exactly Metro_zori_uc_sfrcondomfr_sm_sa_month.csv, because the SA and not-SA files have the same layout and nothing in the content names the variant; (b) the header begins RegionID,SizeRank,RegionName,RegionType,StateName, then month-end date columns that are consecutive and ascending from 2015-01-31; (c) the newest column is the last day of --expected-month; (d) a RegionType 'country' row 'United States' exists, and every frozen universe RegionID is present (a missing one is reported and handled by the drop rule in Missing data); (e) the two newest values are positive numbers for every frozen metro; (f) the variant and continuity check: for each of the ten profile metros, the M-1 change computed inside the new file is within 0.05 percentage points of the M-1 change computed inside the previous archived file. The owner measured within-file revisions of at most 0.02; a failure means the wrong variant was downloaded, or Zillow changed its method, and a maintainer must look; (g) sha256 of the bytes; write-once per capture day; refuse a capture day earlier than the newest archived one (both as in ingest_yougov_xtab.py). Output: archive path, expected month, sha256, created. Access risk: zillow.com pages return a PerimeterX captcha (HTTP 403) to non-browser clients [verified 2026-11-09T01:03:00Z and 01:03:08Z, honest user agent]. A person in a browser gets through; the arena's runners would not, and must not try.
source.archive_policy: Proposed verdict: permission needed. Use allowed? unclear. Manual download by a person: allowed only for personal use in the plain text; for SSA, unclear. Automated retrieval: forbidden. Keeping raw copies: unclear. Public redistribution of the raw file: not permitted. Showing derived numbers with citation: permitted only if the CSVs count as 'Aggregate Data'. Evidence: Zillow Terms of Use, 'Updated October 28, 2025', read from the Internet Archive capture of 2026-02-01, because zillow.com returned a PerimeterX 403 [verified text]. ConductAtlas reports a later version captured 2026-10-16 that it had not compared [unverified]; a person should confirm the live text in a browser. Sorted by fetching, use and redistribution (lesson 10). FETCHING, §5 'Prohibited Use': 'BY USING THE SERVICES, YOU AGREE NOT TO: ... conduct automated queries (including screen and database scraping, spiders, robots, crawlers, bypassing "captcha" or similar precautions, or any other automated activity with the purpose of obtaining information from the Services) on the Services'. 'Services' covers Zillow's 'websites, networks, mobile applications, or other services' (preamble), so this most plausibly includes files.zillowstatic.com, and it rules out a scripted download, including a one-off research fetch. USE AND COPYING, §4.C 'Use of Content': 'you may copy information from the Services without the aid of any automated processes and only as necessary for your personal use or Pro Use to view, save, print, fax and/or e-mail such information. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the aggregate level data provided on the Zillow Local-Info Pages (the "Aggregate Data") may be used for non-personal uses, e.g., real estate market analysis.' REDISTRIBUTION, §4.C continued: 'You may display and distribute derivative works of the Aggregate Data (e.g., within a graph), only so long as the Zillow Companies are cited as a source on every page where the Aggregate Data are displayed, including "Data Provided by Zillow Group." ... You are prohibited from displaying any other Zillow Companies' data without our prior written approval.' §4.A adds: 'Except as expressly stated herein, these Terms of Use do not provide you with a license to use, reproduce, distribute, display or provide access to any portion of the Service'. Separate research-data terms: none found. The Research data page (Internet Archive capture 2026-10-26) says only 'Download Zillow's home value index, rent index, forecasts, for-sale inventory, and other housing data for use in your own analyses.' It shows no licence, no attribution line and no link to separate terms. The owner doc's 'free public use with attribution' is not on that page [unverified; it may sit elsewhere]. What this means for the design: if maintainers read the Research CSVs as Aggregate Data, then (1) a person may download by hand for SSA's analysis, (2) SSA may display derived numbers (each metro's change, the ranking) with 'Data Provided by Zillow Group' on every page that shows them, and (3) the raw CSV must not go in the public repository. YouGov's raw xlsx files are committed publicly under sources/yougov_xtab/; that is not available here. Raw files go to private storage, and the public record is the sha256, the capture day and the derived values. Owner decision (rev 2): ask Zillow Research in writing, and wait. Tasks for a person (G4), in order. (1) A maintainer opens https://www.zillow.com/z/corp/terms/ in a normal browser and checks that §4.A, §4.C and §5 still read as quoted above (the quote is from the 2025-10-28 version; ConductAtlas reports a newer capture of 2026-10-16). (2) The same person opens https://www.zillow.com/research/calendar/ and copies the Market Report and data-update dates for December 2026 to March 2027 into the card. (3) The maintainer, and nobody else on SSA's side, sends this message through the contact route on Zillow Research's site (the agent has not looked up an address): 'We run the Social Simulation Arena, a public, non-commercial research benchmark that scores forecasts of published statistics after they are released. We would like to use the ZORI metro file (Smoothed, Seasonally Adjusted, All Homes Plus Multifamily). (1) Is research use of the Research data downloads covered by the Aggregate Data terms in section 4.C of the Terms of Use, with the citation "Data Provided by Zillow Group"? (2) May a team member download the file by hand once a month and keep each monthly copy unchanged in a private archive, so results can be checked later? (3) May we publish derived numbers (each metro's monthly % change and a top-10 ranking) and the file's SHA-256 hash? (4) Would you allow a script to fetch that one file once a month from files.zillowstatic.com, or should it stay a manual download?' (4) Record the date sent and any reply, verbatim, in this card's evidence. Fallback: if there is no answer by 2026-12-18, this source pauses and the BLS metro rent profile is used instead. Zillow's CPI forecast is not used (bls-cpi-rent rev 2), so the earlier question 5 is dropped.

target.population: Market-rate asking rents on new listings: a repeat-rent index weighted to the whole rental stock, using rents between the 35th and 65th percentiles, smoothed over three months and seasonally adjusted. The cut is 'All Homes Plus Multifamily', which adds buildings with 5+ units to single-family, condo and co-op homes [Research page text, Internet Archive capture 2026-10-26, verified; methodology in the owner doc]. It measures rents on new leases, not what existing tenants pay (that is the bls-cpi-rent card). Q1: the 10 largest metros by SizeRank, frozen at season start; the owner doc lists New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, Dallas, Houston, Washington, Philadelphia, Miami, Atlanta, Boston. Each is identified by its RegionID in the first archived file, not by name, because names can be relabelled. Q2: the 50 largest by SizeRank in that same first file, frozen.
target.window: Month M of Zillow's monthly series (the column labelled with M's month-end date). The file is updated around the 16th of M+1.
target.calculation: For metro r: 100 x (V_r,M / V_r,M-1 - 1), where both values come from the same file, the resolution file. Levels are never compared across files, because Zillow recomputes all history every month: between the September and October 2026 not-SA files, past levels moved by up to 2.2% (Boston), while within-file month-over-month changes moved by at most 0.02 points [owner doc, unverified by the agent]. Q2: rank the frozen 50 that are present by that change, descending, with ties broken by RegionName ascending; take the first ten.
target.unit: Q1: percent, one-month change, SA, ten cells. Q2: an ordered list of ten metros.

lock: 00:00 America/New_York two days before Zillow's Market Report for month M (owner doc rule). The Market Report prints the month's national figure about ten days before the file. Owner-doc dates: October data, Market Report Thu 2026-11-05 (passed); November data, Market Report Fri 2026-12-04, so lock Wed 2026-12-02 00:00 ET. December 2026 data: the Market Report date is not known to the agent. The calendar lists dates about three months ahead, but https://www.zillow.com/research/calendar/ was not fetched, given the 403s and the terms. A person reads it in a browser. If the report falls on about 2027-01-06, the lock is about Mon 2027-01-04 00:00 ET. Unscored pilot (owner decision G3): two rounds, December 2026 data (lock about 2027-01-04, file about 2027-01-16) and January 2027 data (lock about early February 2027, file about 2027-02-16). Both need the rights answer first. The pilot measures the zero point's spread and the SA file's revisions between two consecutive downloads. Earliest realistic first scored lock: February 2027 data, about early March 2027 (two days before that month's Market Report; the date comes from the G4 calendar task). The November round (2026-12-02) cannot work: rights are not settled, the ingest tool and first archived file do not exist, and a change reaching main about 2026-11-24 would leave participants 8 days. Working back from the first pilot lock of 2027-01-04: Zillow's answer, and the ingest tool on main, by about 2026-12-18 (the owner's fallback date). If the rights answer comes later, the first lock moves one month at a time. Lock reference: the newest archived file, which must have newest column M-1 and a capture day after the 16th of M (lesson 13: no file carrying M-1, no round).
baseline: Q1 ranked zero point: per-metro persistence, the M-1 change computed inside the lock file. In the general family (G1) it is mean_k with k = 1 and an rms_n spread with n = 12. The spread is measured, never the default (G2): sd per metro = RMS of persistence's own error over the 12 most recent months, computed inside the lock file, where history is consistent. With the arena's default persistence spread (sd 1.5) on changes whose month-to-month miss is about 0.06 to 0.10 points [owner doc], a normal reference with sd 1.5 has expected CRPS of about 0.35 points. An honest-spread copy of the same mean has about 0.05 to 0.08. So submitting persistence with a realistic spread would score roughly +80% skill for free [inferred analytically from the owner doc's MAE; the same pattern measured +84.6% on CPI rent and +49% on the CPI metro profile]. The lesson-12 check, the reference's best rescale gain and its coverage, is run on the first archived file during the pilot. It is a named gap in open_questions. Also shown, not ranked: the 6-month mean (owner doc: per-metro MAE 0.05 to 0.15, against 0.06 to 0.10 for persistence), the national change put into every metro (owner doc: misses by 0.14), and 50%/90% coverage. Q2 zero point: last month's top ten from the lock file, scored with RBO at p = 0.9, as in the arena's wiki_top10 ranking round. Owner doc: consecutive months' top tens scored RBO 0.43 on average over 36 months and 0.79 over the last 6; 5.6 of 10 names carried over on average.
resolution: The first archived file, by capture day, whose newest column is M and which passed every ingest check. All ten (Q1) or all present universe metros (Q2) are computed inside that file. 'First' is by capture day in the private archive. A later download of the same month, if Zillow corrected the file mid-month, is kept as evidence but never replaces the resolving file. Resolution is posted when the file is ingested. With a download on the 16th to 18th, that is two to four weeks after the lock.
missing_data_policy: (1) Person lapse: round M resolves from any capture whose newest column is M, taken before Zillow's next monthly update (about the 16th of M+2). The file is static between updates, so a late manual download still gives the publisher's month-M file, and the continuity check (f) guards against a mid-month change. If no such capture exists by then, round M is cancelled. Round M+1 then has no lock reference and is refused (lesson 13). (2) Publisher delay: if no file with newest column M has appeared by the 23rd of M+1 (owner doc rule), the round is cancelled, never reopened. The person checks on the 16th to 18th and again on the 23rd, and records 'not yet updated' in the round log. (3) A frozen metro missing from the resolution file: Q1 is cancelled for that month, since the profile is never scored partially. Q2 drops the metro from that round's universe (owner doc rule), and the ranking is computed on the rest. (4) An ingest check fails: nothing is filed, and a maintainer decides within the same window. (5) Zillow changes its method, or the variant check fails twice: rounds pause until the card is revised. Reminders: the arena's watch job (~/ssa-watch) should flag 'no ZORI capture with the expected month by the 18th', as it does for stale YouGov pulls.
scoring: Q1: arena profile scoring, ten cells each as {mean, sd > 0} or quantiles, energy score (scoring.energy_score), reported as level plus structure. Skill = 1 - ES(entrant) / ES(zero point), with the measured-spread persistence reference: mean_k (k = 1) with an rms_n spread (n = 12). This is the same parameterised family as bls-cpi-rent's mean_k (k = 6), so implementation adds one reference, not a name per card (G1). Q2: arena ranking round, an ordered list of ten scored with RBO at p = 0.9 (ssa/ranking_round.py), point-scored by design, as that module documents; skill against last month's list. The owner doc expects small skill scores, as on the Civiqs tasks, because the index is smoothed. Every public page showing these numbers carries 'Data Provided by Zillow Group' and no Zillow logo (ToU §4.C).

It carries no licence, attribution line or link to separate terms. The only ZORI CSV URL in the HTML is the not-SA metro file Metro_zori_uc_sfrcondomfr_sm_month.csv.

The file's layout, size (741 metros in October 2026), dates and all movement figures are the owner's [owner input, unverified]. The first manual download is also the first chance to verify them.

evidence.url: file:urban-track-overview.txt (owner doc, section 'Zillow Observed Rent Index (ZORI)')
evidence.finding: [owner input] US SA MoM: mean 0.22, sd 0.07, persistence miss 0.03. Top-10 metros: SA MoM sd 0.07 to 0.19, persistence miss 0.06 to 0.10, 6-month-mean miss 0.05 to 0.15. Cross-metro spread sd 0.16, against 0.08 month to month. Revisions: past levels move up to 2.2% between files, within-file changes at most 0.02 points (measured on the not-SA file only; the doc asks for the SA file to be re-measured with the November file). Calendar: file on the 16th; Market Report around the 5th.

[verified] The model for the manual route: it parses the local file, refuses a newest wave other than --expected-wave, requires every cell, files write-once per UTC capture day, refuses back-dated capture days and same-day different bytes, and prints sha256. tools/pull_yougov_xtab.py fetches by script when a person runs it with --execute. That is not available for Zillow, where even a person-triggered script is an automated query; Zillow must be a browser download.

[provenance] Dataset owner and author of the doc section 'Zillow Observed Rent Index (ZORI)': Mingyi He <mingyihe@mit.edu> (Urban Track contributor list). Card drafted by the SSA Track Agent (Claude). Revision 2 owner decisions: Claude, delegated by Haoyang Shang, 2026-11-08. Recorded here until card.py has an owner field.

open_questions: Blocking, waiting on a person: Zillow Research's written answer to the message in Source (archive_policy). It is sent by an SSA maintainer, and nobody else sends anything. If there is no answer by 2026-12-18, the owner's fallback applies: this card pauses and the ten-metro BLS CPI rent profile (bls-cpi-rent future work) becomes the metro rent target.

Named measurement gap, closed by the pilot: the zero point's measured spread (persistence, rms_12, computed inside the lock file) and its lesson-12 check (best gain from rescaling the reference's sd; 50%/90% coverage) can only be computed on the first manually downloaded file. The card cannot be approved for scoring until the pilot has filled in these numbers.
assumptions: Owner decisions, wave 2 (Claude, delegated by Haoyang Shang, 2026-11-08; file DECISIONS-wave2.md). Rights A: a person asks Zillow Research and work waits; fallback C, the BLS metro rent profile, if there is no answer by 2026-12-18 (runner-up B, launching on the maintainers' own reading of §4.C, was not chosen). Questions A: Q1 ten-metro profile plus Q2 top-10 ranking. Lock A: the doc's 00:00 ET two days before the Market Report (runner-up B, the last day of month M). Browser download only.

Card status stays in_review, not draft. The design is complete on the manual route, and the blockers are named in open_questions (lesson 6 pattern). Runner-up: draft, because the data sample is unverified.

Not downloading the CSV during research. Reason: ToU §5 bars 'any other automated activity with the purpose of obtaining information', and a curl fetch is one. Runner-up: one scripted fetch as a 'sample', rejected. The owner's own downloaded copies, or the first manual pull, verify the numbers.

Raw files in private storage, not the public repo. Reason: §4.C allows displaying derivative works of Aggregate Data only, and §4.A grants no licence to distribute otherwise. Runner-up: public, as YouGov; only if Zillow agrees in writing (question 3 of the message in Source).

Late manual pulls are allowed until Zillow's next update, not cancelled at the 23rd. Reason: the file is static between updates, so a late person-pull returns the publisher's month-M file, and cancelling for a lapse wastes a scored round. The owner doc's 23rd rule is kept for publisher delay. Runner-up: a hard 23rd deadline for both, which is simpler.

Continuity tolerance 0.05 points (check f), chosen by the agent: 2.5 times the owner's measured maximum within-file revision of 0.02, and below the SA/not-SA gap in any month with seasonality. Runner-up: 0.03. Re-measure on the first two SA files.

Suggested arena names, for implementation: tracker 'zillow_zori'; series 'zori_sa_mom_<regionid>'; private archive sources-private/zillow_zori/<YYYY-MM-DD>.csv (the location is a maintainer choice); tools/ingest_zori.py; round_ids 'zori-<YYYY-MM>-metro10' and 'zori-<YYYY-MM>-top10'. Naming changes no rule.
